title: ANSMET: Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search with Near-Memory Processing and Hybrid Early Termination
problem: Approximate nearest neighbor search (ANNS) over large high-dimensional vector databases is both highly memory-bound and computationally wasteful: a large fraction of fetched vectors and their distance computations are ultimately discarded because many candidate vectors are far from the query. This dual inefficiency — excess memory traffic and low data utilization — limits throughput and energy efficiency on general-purpose computing platforms.
method: ANSMET co-designs a near-data processing (NDP) architecture at the memory rank level with a hybrid partial-dimension/bit early termination strategy. Distance calculation and comparison for ANNS are offloaded to near-data units within memory ranks, eliminating main memory bandwidth consumption for rejected vectors. As a vector is streamed from memory, ANSMET conservatively estimates a lower-bound distance using partial dimensions and/or partial bits of each element; if this lower bound already exceeds a threshold, the fetch and computation are terminated early. Data layout within a single memory access and across multiple memory ranks is co-optimized to match the early termination granularity, and a lightweight host-NDP coordination protocol manages index traversal and result sorting.

title: BlasPart: A Deterministic Parallel Partitioner for Balanced Large-Scale Hypergraph Partitioning
problem: Balanced hypergraph partitioning for large-scale systems (VLSI, HPC) must scale to thousands of partitions while maintaining high partition quality and deterministic outputs.
method: BlasPart employs recursive multilevel bisection framework for deterministic parallel partitioning. Level-dependent balance constraints improve efficiency and effectiveness. Parallel algorithm maintains deterministic output (reproducibility across runs). Designed for 4096-way partitioning on large industrial benchmarks.

title: High Energy-efficiency and Low latency In-Memory Computing using Analog Accumulator and In-Memory ADC with shared References
problem: In-memory computing array ADCs require high area overhead for data conversion; traditional approaches sacrifice linearity and energy efficiency.
method: A 256x128 in-memory array uses dual-8T SRAM bitcells for ternary weight storage and read-write decoupling. Bit-slicing with charge-sharing binary weighted accumulator (CHA) handles multi-bit input. Read WWL Under Drive enables low-current variation.

title: A Post-Implementation Performance Prediction Method with HLS Optimization Directives
problem: High-Level Synthesis (HLS) performance prediction methods fail to capture complex directive-hardware interactions and resource reuse issues, leading to inaccurate timing and power predictions for directive-optimized circuits.
method: The method integrates a Graph Builder that encodes directive optimization and resource reuse into graph representations, then applies a TransformerConv-based Graph Neural Network with an aggregation pool module to capture timing-critical features and predict critical path delay, power, and resource utilization.

title: X-ray Ptychography at the Edge: Towards Real-Time Feedback for High-Speed Nanoimaging
problem: X-ray ptychography requires computationally intensive iterative reconstruction algorithms, and recent advances in data acquisition have dramatically increased data generation rates, making real-time reconstruction challenging.
method: GPU-based iterative reconstruction algorithms deployed at the edge with efficient implementation enabling real-time processing during high-speed continuous data acquisition.

title: MagiCache: A Virtual In-Cache Computing Engine
problem: Array-level in-cache computing architectures dedicate entire cache arrays as compute arrays, leaving most computing lines idle at runtime while the non-computing arrays absorb large bursty memory accesses—both causing severe on-chip capacity loss and high data movement latency for data-parallel applications.
method: MagiCache introduces cacheline-level in-cache computing: each cache array can dynamically configure individual rows as either computing lines or cachelines with negligible hardware overhead. A virtual engine monitors runtime computation and storage requirements and dynamically reallocates rows within each array between compute and cache roles via cacheline-level space management. An instruction chaining technique enables asynchronous execution of computing arrays, overlapping bursty HBM/DRAM access latency with ongoing computation through pipelined, out-of-order scheduling of memory requests and compute operations.

title: Tackling the Challenges of Adding Pulse-level Support to a Heterogeneous HPCQC Software Stack: MQSS Pulse
problem: Heterogeneous HPC-Quantum Computing (HPCQC) software stacks lack native pulse-level control, limiting quantum program expressiveness and hardware utilization. Pulse-level abstractions (ports, frames, waveforms) are not integrated into standard HPC-QC environments.
method: MQSS Pulse: Extension of Munich Quantum Software Stack with native pulse-level support. Introduces compiled C/C++ pulse API (avoiding Python overhead), extends LLVM for pulse instructions, uses C-based backend interface for hardware constraints, and designs portable pulse exchange format.

title: XShift: FPGA-efficient Binarized LLM with Joint Quantization and Sparsification
problem: LLM binarization severely degrades activation precision and fails to eliminate multipliers from self-attention; LLMs show stage-specific (prefill vs decode) computational imbalance requiring specialized handling.
method: XShift combines three innovations: (1) XNOR-Shift Encoding (XSE) replacing multiplications with XNOR and shifts, (2) Hardware Adaptive Outlier and Sparsity (HAOS) exploiting channel distributions and systolic arrays, (3) XNOR-Shift Systolic Array (XSSA) + Base-2 SoftMax Converter (BSMC) for binarized compute.

title: Cosmological Hydrodynamics at Exascale: A Trillion-Particle Leap in Capability
problem: Cosmological simulations require matching the scale, fidelity, and physical complexity of next-generation sky surveys, demanding exascale simulation of multi-trillion particles with self-consistent gas dynamics and gravity.
method: CRK-HACC: cosmological hydrodynamics code using separation-of-scale techniques, GPU-resident tree solvers, in situ analysis pipelines, and multi-tiered I/O strategies for extreme scalability on Frontier supercomputer.

title: MoE-Lightning: High-Throughput MoE Inference on Memory-constrained GPUs
problem: Sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) LLMs have very large total parameter counts that exceed the VRAM of commodity GPUs, forcing weight offloading to CPU memory or NVMe, which creates severe I/O bottlenecks and low GPU utilization during batch inference.
method: MoE-Lightning introduces CGOPipe (CPU-GPU-I/O Pipelining) with paged weight management: expert weights are stored in pages that are streamed between CPU memory and GPU memory in a pipeline overlapping expert computation with prefetching of the next expert's weights. A Hierarchical Roofline Model (HRM) performance model guides policy selection by predicting throughput as a function of batch size, GPU memory, CPU memory, and I/O bandwidth. The system supports multi-GPU configurations for even larger models (Mixtral 8x22B, DBRX) on 2-4 T4 GPUs.

title: Everactive: Self-Powered SoC with Energy Harvesting, Wakeup Receiver, and Energy-Aware Subsystem
problem: Battery-powered IoT and edge devices suffer from limited lifetime; Everactive proposes a self-powered SoC that harvests ambient energy (RF, thermal, mechanical) to enable continuous operation without battery replacement.
method: Everactive integrates energy harvesting circuits (RF rectifier, thermoelectric, piezoelectric), a wakeup receiver for low-power event detection, and an energy-aware subsystem that dynamically manages compute and memory based on harvested power availability.

title: An Innovative Solution to Improve Ultra Low Voltage Writability and Leakage in GPU SRAMs
problem: GPU SRAM scaling to 3nm fails at ultra-low voltage (ULV); write failures and high leakage due to bit-cell scaling
method: Innovative circuit solutions in 3nm SRAM for ULV write-ability and leakage reduction

title: 17.6 A 100MHz Self-Calibrating RC Oscillator Capable of Clock-Glitch Detection for Hardware Security in a 3nm FinFET Process
problem: On-chip oscillators are needed for SoC security functions (boot-up, external clock attack detection), but existing designs either provide stable clocks without glitch detection or detect glitches without maintaining stability—no prior design achieves both.
method: Self-calibrating RC oscillator in 3nm FinFET with dual-mode operation: stable 100MHz clock generation via self-calibration and hardware-integrated clock-glitch detection circuit that can identify fault injection attacks on critical system clocks.

title: AI Agents for Enabling Autonomous Experiments at ORNL's HPC and Manufacturing User Facilities
problem: Scientific experimentation across heterogeneous HPC and manufacturing facilities requires manual coordination, limiting throughput and hindering rapid iteration. Lack of automation prevents tight coupling between experimental and computational workflows.
method: Modular AI-agent architecture integrating: (1) natural language interface via LLM, (2) multi-agent framework for decision-making, (3) programmable facility APIs, (4) provenance-aware workflow infrastructure. Demonstrated on additive manufacturing experiments with real-time HPC coordination.

title: MARIO: A Superadditive Multi-Algorithm Interworking Optimization Framework for Analog Circuit Sizing
problem: Analog circuit sizing involves expensive simulations, non-linearity, and high dimensionality; diverse circuit types have different optimization landscapes, making single-algorithm approaches sub-optimal.
method: MARIO combines a pool of optimization algorithms via multi-algorithm interworking protocol achieving superadditivity. Uses multitask Gaussian process regression and portfolio optimization for online resource reallocation. Includes evaluation data broadcast for cross-algorithm cooperation and asynchronous parallelization for algorithms with different computational costs.

title: TOGGLE6.0: A 4.8Gbps Next Generation Area and Power Efficient Transceiver for Flash Memory Interface
problem: Flash memory interfaces (UFS in mobile phones) require high-speed data transfer (4.8 Gbps) with stringent constraints on area and power. Current transceiver designs suffer from excessive pad capacitance, device stress, and timing margins, limiting performance and increasing area footprint.
method: Toggle6.0 scalable transceiver architecture using: (1) thin-oxide devices to reduce pad capacitance; (2) elevated ground voltage generator to reduce device stress on drivers; (3) multi-tap current-based equalization for signal integrity with minimal area; (4) per-receiver VREF-based tuning for timing margin improvement.
